heading: INT. CONVERTED GRAIN SILO - ARBITRATION HALL - DAY

units.text: INT. CONVERTED GRAIN SILO - ARBITRATION HALL - DAY
A round concrete chamber, forty feet across, with a ladder bolted to the wall and a hopper chute high above.
A plank bench for the public.
A folding table for the court.
Dust floats in a single shaft of light.
JUDGE PHAEDRA LOMAX, 60s, in a rumpled black robe over a flannel shirt, sits behind the table.
She keeps a thermos of tea at her elbow and a gavel carved from a fence post.
SIMONE DUCHAMP, 40s, lead counsel for the farmers, in a tailored green suit, rises, a stack of exhibits hugged to her chest.
TARIQ NASSAR, 40s, counsel for the agribusiness, in a charcoal suit and silk tie, taps his pen against his notepad.
CLETUS WREN, 60s, the bailiff, stands at the ladder with his thumbs hooked in his belt.
He has not smiled since the Carter administration.
In a single armchair at the side sits the FOREMAN, 50s, a man in overalls and a seed-company cap, with a clipboard in his lap.
He chews a toothpick.
We are on the record. Ms. Duchamp.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Your Honour, we ask the jury for a verdict on count one.
units.name: DUCHAMP

units.text: There is no jury, Ms. Duchamp. There is Mr. Foreman.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Then we ask the Foreman.
units.name: DUCHAMP

units.text: Ma'am, I got a question first.
units.name: FOREMAN

units.text: Proceed.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Do I have to say it out loud?
units.name: FOREMAN

units.text: That is how verdicts work.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Even if it makes someone mad?
units.name: FOREMAN

units.text: Especially then.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: He removes the cap.
Smooths his hair.
Puts the cap back on.
Your Honour, I object. The witness is stalling.
units.name: NASSAR

units.text: He is not a witness, Mr. Nassar. Sit down.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: I'd like it noted for the record that--
units.name: NASSAR

units.text: Noted. Sit.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: He sits.
Duchamp's grip on her exhibits tightens.
Mr. Foreman, take your time.
units.name: DUCHAMP

units.text: Don't need it, ma'am.
units.name: FOREMAN

units.text: He stands.
Clears his throat.
The toothpick rolls to the side of his mouth.
On count one, the soil contamination, we find for the farmers.
units.name: FOREMAN

units.text: A murmur on the bench.
Nassar's pen stops.
Duchamp closes her eyes.
Order.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Your Honour, I demand the jury be polled.
units.name: NASSAR

units.text: There is one man, Mr. Nassar. He just spoke.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Then I demand he be re-sworn.
units.name: NASSAR

units.text: Mr. Wren, please re-swear Mr. Foreman.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Raise your right hand.
units.name: WREN

units.text: The Foreman raises his hand.
Wren raises his, solemn.
Do you swear to render a true verdict according to the evidence?
units.name: WREN

units.text: I do.
units.name: FOREMAN

units.text: State your name for the record.
units.name: WREN

units.text: Hiram Stroud.
units.name: FOREMAN

units.text: Hiram Stroud, Dutch Creek. Third generation on the same acres.
units.name: HIRAM

units.text: Thank you, Mr. Stroud. Please repeat your verdict.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: On count one we find for the farmers.
units.name: HIRAM

units.text: He's biased. His own land is in the class.
units.name: NASSAR

units.text: It is. And it's poisoned, sir. I tested it myself.
units.name: HIRAM

units.text: Nassar half rises, shoulders squared.
Hiram does not move.
Wren steps forward.
Duchamp slides between them.
The shaft of light falls across all four faces.
Sit down, Mr. Nassar.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: He does.
He opens his notepad.
Closes it.
Opens it again.
Ms. Duchamp. Count two.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: The farmers move for punitive damages.
units.name: DUCHAMP

units.text: We find for the farmers on count two.
units.name: HIRAM

units.text: You haven't heard the evidence!
units.name: NASSAR

units.text: I've heard four weeks of it. My ears are tired.
units.name: HIRAM

units.text: God bless the plain-spoken.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Wren shifts his weight and says nothing.
The gavel comes down once.
We stand adjourned. Mr. Wren, open the doors.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: He hauls on the silo's iron door.
Light pours in, wheat-gold.
The farmers on the bench rise and file out, caps in their hands.
